prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = (x + 1)(x - 5)$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex of the graph of $f$?
hint: Factored form hands you the zeros. The vertex sits exactly between them.

hints.text: Factored form hands you the zeros. The vertex sits exactly between them.

learningObjective: Locate the axis of symmetry as the midpoint of the zeros.
explanation: Setting each factor to zero gives the $x$-intercepts $x = -1$ and $x = 5$.
A parabola is symmetric, so its vertex lies halfway between the zeros.

alternativeExplanations.title: Or expand and use −b/2a
steps: Averaging the zeros is faster when the quadratic is already factored; $-b/2a$ is the general tool.
